key_insight: Neural approximation power alone does not ensure PINN convergence; discrete stability and accurate comparison networks within admissible trial classes are also needed.
engineering_relevance: For linear elliptic Dirichlet PDEs, the framework guides collocation density and scale-dependent boundary weighting so discrete residual losses can control solution error.
method: Extend kernel collocation theory using elliptic regularity, discrete stability, and consistency.
Identify stable admissible neural subclasses and quantify collocation requirements with physics-balanced boundary weights.

evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence results for tanh-MLPs, not numerical benchmarks or empirical performance measurements.
watch_item: Unconstrained PINN convergence remains conditional under joint network and sampling refinement; approximation estimates alone do not establish the required stability and consistency.
